analysis:
This PR changes only documentation.
- docs/provider/attestation.md: appends a note at lines 325-327. It says local cache-volume checks are storage-suitability checks, not firmware authenticity evidence, and are not part of the coordinator attestation verdict. No change to the TB-009/TB-011 serving-authorization semantics.
- docs/provider/cache-storage.md (new): documents `darkbloom cache set --daily-write-gb/--directory/--reset-directory` and `cache status`. Preconditions: APFS (Encrypted) volume, ownership enabled, private 0700 directory, volume UUID pinned, and `provider.toml` kept on trusted local storage.
- docs/provider/cli-reference.md: adds the `cache` command section and the precedence rule that a saved `[cache].daily_write_gb` overrides `DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_SSD_MAX_WRITE_GB_PER_DAY`. `0` means unlimited.
- The implementing Swift code (Cache/CacheCommand.swift, CacheConfiguration.swift) is not in the diff. Path validation, symlink handling, a TOCTOU window between the check and use, key storage location, and cleanup on reset were not reviewed.
- Findings: one low-severity threat-model gap. Removable cache storage and retention limits touch T-041, A-001 and TB-003. T-041 was oversized and not visible, so what it already covers is unknown.
- No coordinator, authorization, billing or encryption-hop changes. The next pass should examine the cache implementation for the symlink/ownership/volume-swap checks and for whether cache keys stay off the external volume.

findings.detail: docs/provider/cache-storage.md documents a new operator-selected external/separate volume for encrypted SSD prefix-cache payloads, which are derived from consumer prompts (A-001). The same page states that expiry cannot delete files on detached or previously selected disks, and that `--reset-directory` and re-selecting a disk leave old files in place. The result is a retention and exfiltration surface outside the internal disk. It consists of detached media, a volume-UUID pin, `provider.toml` as a trust anchor, and the operator's choice of removable hardware with unverified firmware. Visible threat-model text does not cover this. The T-041 cache entry was too large to inspect here, so I could not confirm whether it already covers it. The PR is docs-only, so I could not verify in code that payloads stay HMAC-keyed and encrypted with keys kept off the removable volume. Fix: add a TB-003/T-041 entry for external cache volumes with their residual risks (orphaned ciphertext, attacker-swapped volumes, a tampered `provider.toml` redirecting the cache, unlimited daily writes). Confirm in the implementing PR that keys never reside on the cache volume.
findings.title: Removable-disk cache option is not reflected in the threat model (A-001 / T-041)
